topic: MBA Reports: Porter's, SWOT & Financial Ratios

copy.instagram:
Staring at a blank SWOT table for your MBA report? We’ve all been there—late night, caffeine wearing off, and that sinking feeling that you’re just stating the obvious. 

Most students fall into the 2:2 trap: listing bullet points that don’t actually talk to each other. You’re not writing a shopping list; you’re writing a strategy.

Slide 1: The Trap. Listing generic strengths and threats without showing how they impact the bottom line. It’s surface-level, and markers see right through it.

Slide 2: The 1st Class Blueprint. This is where you win. Cross-analyze your VRIO competencies against PESTLE risks. Then, back it up with hard data—ROIC, EBITDA, and a realistic, budgeted roadmap. 

Stop guessing what your professor wants and start building a narrative that makes sense to a CEO. 

Save this for your next strategic management deadline. If you’re feeling stuck, check the link in our bio to see how we help get these reports over the line.

copy.facebook:
MBA students, let’s talk about strategic reports. We see so many students lose marks not because they don't understand the concepts, but because they treat frameworks like SWOT and PESTLE as separate boxes to tick.

Here is the shift you need to make for a First Class grade:

• The 2:2 Trap: Listing bullet points without connecting them. If your SWOT doesn't link to your financial analysis, it’s just filler.
• The 1st Class Blueprint: Integrate your VRIO core competencies with your macro-environment (PESTLE). Most importantly, ground your recommendations in real numbers—use ROIC and EBITDA to prove your strategy is actually viable.

Stop stressing over vague feedback and start writing like a consultant. If you’re currently staring at a blinking cursor and need a hand structuring your argument, we’re here to help.
